articles.previewHtml:
Cambodia is a small and recent source of arrivals in Ireland, mostly students on scholarships or self-funded master's courses, hospitality and restaurant workers, and a few professionals in tech and development organisations. Irish NGO and church links with Cambodia go back a long way, and some people come through those networks or through family already in Europe. Phnom Penh's young, internationally minded graduates increasingly look beyond Australia to English-speaking EU options. What surprises most Cambodians first is the cold and the wind, and the way Irish people cheerfully carry on outdoors regardless of the rain.

Quick factsCambodia to Ireland
Visa to enterYes, long stay D visa
Permission to stay beyond 90 daysYes, needs a permit or scheme, then an IRP
Cambodian licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementNo
Social security agreementNo
PetsUnlisted country, rabies blood test

Do you need a visa?

Yes. Cambodian citizens are visa required, so you need an Irish visa before you travel and then an immigration permission to stay. For a move the visa is a long stay D visa, applied for online through AVATS and submitted with your passport and documents to the Irish embassy or visa office that covers Cambodia, or through its VFS partner where one is used. Allow at least eight weeks. The visa gets you to the border; your permission to live here comes from the permit, course or family relationship behind it. You cannot enter on a short stay C visa and switch to a work permission from inside Ireland.

  • Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit, and you can apply for Stamp 4 after two years.
  • General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants, home carers, chefs and construction trades come in on this permit.
  • Stamp 2 study permission for a degree or a recognised English language course, with the right to work 20 hours a week in term time (40 in the holidays). Graduates of Irish degrees get the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) to look for work for one to two years.
  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere. If you have an Irish born parent or grandparent, check the Foreign Births Register first, because once registered you are an Irish citizen and none of the above applies.

Finding work and getting your qualifications recognised

English proficiency varies: many young Cambodian graduates and hospitality workers speak it well, while others need time to build confidence. Employers judge English in interviews rather than through IELTS, but universities and registration bodies usually want a certificate. Irish is on signs but not needed.

Because most routes need a job offer first, the search happens from home. Irish CVs run to two pages, carry no photo and no date of birth, and lead with what you did rather than your job title. Most hiring runs through LinkedIn, IrishJobs, Jobs.ie and the employers' own sites; agencies are strong in tech, finance, pharma and healthcare, and employers used to sponsoring permits say so in the advert. Get your degree assessed by NARIC Ireland (free, through QQI) before you apply; it maps a Cambodian qualification onto the Irish framework and employers recognise the letter. Regulated professions register with their own body: nurses with NMBI, doctors with the Medical Council, teachers with the Teaching Council, engineers with Engineers Ireland, and physiotherapists, radiographers and social workers with CORU. Those bodies, not employers, are the ones that ask for an English test.

Your driving licence

Cambodia is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so you cannot swap a Cambodian licence for an Irish one. You can drive on your Cambodian licence for up to 12 months as a visitor, ideally with an International Driving Permit, but once you are resident you must go through the Irish process: pass the driver theory test, get a learner permit, complete Essential Driver Training and pass the driving test. The good news is that experienced foreign licence holders only need 6 EDT lessons instead of 12 and can skip the usual six month wait before the test. Learner permit holders must be accompanied by a full licence holder, which is the part that catches people out. Remember that Ireland drives on the left.

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and Cambodia have no double taxation agreement. For most people this matters less than it sounds: once you become Irish tax resident (183 days in a tax year, or 280 over two) and your job is here, Irish PAYE applies to your salary and your Cambodian tax obligations usually end with your residence there. It matters if you keep Cambodian income, such as rent or a business, which could be taxed in both countries; Revenue may grant unilateral relief for foreign tax paid, and a tax adviser is worth it in that case. Register with Revenue through myAccount as soon as you have a PPS number.

Check whether your Cambodian state pension can be paid to you in Ireland, and whether you can keep contributing voluntarily from abroad.

Your credit history does not follow you. Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so expect to build a record from scratch before a mortgage or car loan. Moving money from the riel and the US dollar into euro is cheapest through a specialist transfer provider rather than a bank; open the Irish account first, because you need an Irish IBAN to receive salary.

Ireland has a public system run by the HSE, but it is not free at the point of use. A GP visit costs roughly 50 to 70 euro unless you qualify for a medical card or GP visit card on income grounds (children under 8 get GP visits free), and prescriptions are paid for up to a monthly cap under the Drugs Payment Scheme. Emergency departments charge 100 euro without a GP referral. Students, Stamp 0 holders and most visa applicants must show private medical insurance, so many people arrive with a policy already.

Around half the population holds private health insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health, mainly to shorten waiting lists. If you are 35 or older, buy it within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading. Register with a GP as soon as you have an address; practices in Dublin often have closed lists, so ask several.

Goods arriving from Cambodia are imports from outside the EU. You can bring your household belongings free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for at least 12 months and owned the goods for at least 6 months; your removals company files the declaration and you cannot sell the goods for a year. A car qualifies for VRT relief on the same terms, but shipping a car from Cambodia rarely makes sense once freight, registration and Irish insurance are added up.

Cambodia is an unlisted country under the EU pet rules, which adds a blood test. Your dog, cat or ferret needs a microchip, then a rabies vaccination, then a rabies antibody titre test at least 30 days after the vaccination at an EU approved laboratory, and then a three month wait from the date of the blood sample before travel. Add an EU animal health certificate issued within 10 days of travel and, for dogs, a tapeworm treatment 24 to 120 hours before arrival. Pets must arrive as manifest cargo or with an approved airline on an approved route (Dublin Airport handles most). Start the process at least four months before you fly.

Settling in: community and daily life

The Cambodian community in Ireland is very small and recent, concentrated in Dublin with a scattering of students in Cork and Galway. Newcomers usually connect through wider Southeast Asian groups, Buddhist gatherings, university international societies and WhatsApp groups, and often rely on Thai, Vietnamese and Filipino networks for food and friendship.

Phnom Penh's heat and short, sharp downpours give way to cool damp weather in every season and dark winter afternoons. Renting is formal and competitive, food and eating out cost far more, and street food and late-night markets barely exist. Cards are used for nearly everything, and driving is on the left rather than the right.

There are no regular direct flights between Dublin and Cambodia, so getting home usually means one stop, most often via Dubai, Doha, Abu Dhabi, Istanbul, London or Amsterdam; budget for the time as well as the fare.

  • Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie with your passport and proof of Irish address.
  • Register for your Irish Residence Permit within 90 days (300 euro); book the appointment the week you land because slots fill up.
  • Register with Revenue myAccount once you have a PPS number so your employer can tax you correctly.
  • Open an Irish bank account; a utility bill, tenancy agreement or employer letter usually counts as proof of address.
  • Register with a GP and, if you want it, buy private health insurance within 9 months.
  • Get a Leap card for public transport and book the driver theory test if you plan to drive.
  • If a pet is following later, get its rabies blood test done now so the three month clock is running.

Ireland's reputation for friendliness and its smaller scale appeal to those seeking an alternative to London or the US. Social security agreementYes, bilateral agreement
Working Holiday AuthorisationYes
PetsListed country, no blood test

Do you need a visa?

Japanese citizens are not visa required, so you can enter Ireland for up to 90 days without applying for anything. Staying longer is a different matter: you need an immigration permission before the 90 days run out, and you cannot turn a visit into a job from inside the country except through a handful of schemes.   • General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants, home carers, chefs and construction trades come in on this permit.

  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.
  • Stamp 0 for retirees and people of independent means, with income of around 50,000 euro a year per person and private medical insurance, and no right to work.

Those bodies, not employers, are the ones that ask for an English test.

Kazakhstan is a small but growing source of arrivals in Ireland, with students on postgraduate scholarships in engineering, finance, IT and public policy leading the way, followed by professionals in tech, energy services, finance and academia. Graduates from Almaty and Astana see Ireland as an English-speaking EU base with strong tech and financial services sectors. Some arrive after studying in the UK, and family and marriage bring others. What surprises most Kazakhs first is the absence of a real winter: no deep snow or hard frost, just months of grey drizzle and wind.

Quick factsKazakhstan to Ireland
Visa to enterYes, long stay D visa
Permission to stay beyond 90 daysYes, needs a permit or scheme, then an IRP
Kazakh licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementYes
Social security agreementNo
PetsUnlisted country, rabies blood test

Do you need a visa?

Yes. Kazakh citizens are visa required, so you need an Irish visa before you travel and then an immigration permission to stay. For a move the visa is a long stay D visa, applied for online through AVATS and submitted with your passport and documents to the Irish embassy or visa office that covers Kazakhstan, or through its VFS partner where one is used. Allow at least eight weeks. The visa gets you to the border; your permission to live here comes from the permit, course or family relationship behind it. You cannot enter on a short stay C visa and switch to a work permission from inside Ireland.

  • Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit, and you can apply for Stamp 4 after two years.
  • General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants, home carers, chefs and construction trades come in on this permit.
  • Stamp 2 study permission for a degree or a recognised English language course, with the right to work 20 hours a week in term time (40 in the holidays). Graduates of Irish degrees get the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) to look for work for one to two years.
  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere. If you have an Irish born parent or grandparent, check the Foreign Births Register first, because once registered you are an Irish citizen and none of the above applies.

Finding work and getting your qualifications recognised

English levels among Kazakh students and professionals are usually good, often alongside Kazakh and Russian, though Irish accents and idiom take time. Employers rarely ask for IELTS, but universities and professional registration bodies usually do. Irish appears on signs but is not needed.

Because most routes need a job offer first, the search happens from home. Irish CVs run to two pages, carry no photo and no date of birth, and lead with what you did rather than your job title. Most hiring runs through LinkedIn, IrishJobs, Jobs.ie and the employers' own sites; agencies are strong in tech, finance, pharma and healthcare, and employers used to sponsoring permits say so in the advert. Get your degree assessed by NARIC Ireland (free, through QQI) before you apply; it maps a Kazakh qualification onto the Irish framework and employers recognise the letter. Regulated professions register with their own body: nurses with NMBI, doctors with the Medical Council, teachers with the Teaching Council, engineers with Engineers Ireland, and physiotherapists, radiographers and social workers with CORU. Those bodies, not employers, are the ones that ask for an English test.

Your driving licence

Kazakhstan is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so you cannot swap a Kazakh licence for an Irish one. You can drive on your Kazakh licence for up to 12 months as a visitor, ideally with an International Driving Permit, but once you are resident you must go through the Irish process: pass the driver theory test, get a learner permit, complete Essential Driver Training and pass the driving test. The good news is that experienced foreign licence holders only need 6 EDT lessons instead of 12 and can skip the usual six month wait before the test. Learner permit holders must be accompanied by a full licence holder, which is the part that catches people out. Remember that Ireland drives on the left.

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and Kazakhstan have a double taxation agreement, so income taxed in one country is generally credited in the other and the treaty decides which country taxes what. You become Irish tax resident after 183 days in a tax year (or 280 days over two years), and from then Ireland taxes your worldwide income, with credit for Kazakh tax under the treaty. Register with Revenue through myAccount as soon as you have a PPS number so your employer taxes you correctly, and tell the Kazakh tax authority that you are leaving.

There is no social security agreement between Ireland and Kazakhstan, so the two records stand alone. You need at least 520 paid PRSI contributions (ten years) to qualify for any Irish State Pension (Contributory), and the full rate takes 40 years of contributions. Check whether your Kazakh state pension can be paid to you in Ireland, and whether you can keep contributing voluntarily from abroad.

Your credit history does not follow you. Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so expect to build a record from scratch before a mortgage or car loan. Moving money from the tenge into euro is cheapest through a specialist transfer provider rather than a bank; open the Irish account first, because you need an Irish IBAN to receive salary.

Healthcare

Ireland has a public system run by the HSE, but it is not free at the point of use. Once you are ordinarily resident (living in Ireland or intending to for at least a year) you use public hospitals as a public patient, and inpatient charges were abolished in April 2023. A GP visit costs roughly 50 to 70 euro unless you qualify for a medical card or GP visit card on income grounds (children under 8 get GP visits free), and prescriptions are paid for up to a monthly cap under the Drugs Payment Scheme. Emergency departments charge 100 euro without a GP referral. Students, Stamp 0 holders and most visa applicants must show private medical insurance, so many people arrive with a policy already.

Around half the population holds private health insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health, mainly to shorten waiting lists. If you are 35 or older, buy it within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading. Register with a GP as soon as you have an address; practices in Dublin often have closed lists, so ask several.

Bringing your things and your pet

Goods arriving from Kazakhstan are imports from outside the EU. You can bring your household belongings free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for at least 12 months and owned the goods for at least 6 months; your removals company files the declaration and you cannot sell the goods for a year. A car qualifies for VRT relief on the same terms, but shipping a car from Kazakhstan rarely makes sense once freight, registration and Irish insurance are added up.

Kazakhstan is an unlisted country under the EU pet rules, which adds a blood test. Your dog, cat or ferret needs a microchip, then a rabies vaccination, then a rabies antibody titre test at least 30 days after the vaccination at an EU approved laboratory, and then a three month wait from the date of the blood sample before travel. Add an EU animal health certificate issued within 10 days of travel and, for dogs, a tapeworm treatment 24 to 120 hours before arrival. Pets must arrive as manifest cargo or with an approved airline on an approved route (Dublin Airport handles most). Start the process at least four months before you fly.

Settling in: community and daily life

The Kazakh community in Ireland is small and recent, almost entirely in Dublin with students in Cork, Galway and Limerick. Newcomers connect through wider Central Asian and Russian-speaking networks, university international societies, Nauryz celebrations organised by students, mosque communities, and Telegram and WhatsApp groups.

Kazakhstan's dry continental extremes give way to a mild, damp climate where the difference between seasons is mostly daylight and rain. Renting is formal and competitive, groceries and eating out cost more, and portions of meat are smaller. Cards dominate as at home, driving is on the left, and pubs rather than home gatherings are where colleagues meet.

There are no regular direct flights between Dublin and Kazakhstan, so getting home usually means one stop, most often via Dubai, Doha, Abu Dhabi, Istanbul, London or Amsterdam; budget for the time as well as the fare.

First 30 days checklist

  • Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie with your passport and proof of Irish address.
  • Register for your Irish Residence Permit within 90 days (300 euro); book the appointment the week you land because slots fill up.
  • Register with Revenue myAccount once you have a PPS number so your employer can tax you correctly.
  • Open an Irish bank account; a utility bill, tenancy agreement or employer letter usually counts as proof of address.
  • Register with a GP and, if you want it, buy private health insurance within 9 months.
  • Get a Leap card for public transport and book the driver theory test if you plan to drive.
  • If a pet is following later, get its rabies blood test done now so the three month clock is running.

★ Useful links

  • Immigration Service Delivery: visas and permissions
  • Employment permits
  • NARIC Ireland: qualification recognition
  • National Driver Licence Service
  • Revenue: moving to Ireland
  • Department of Agriculture: bringing your pet to Ireland
  • Health Insurance Authority

Irish aid and university links with Laos bring some students directly to Dublin, Cork and Galway, while others arrive after study in Thailand, Australia or elsewhere. Young Lao graduates value Ireland as a friendly English-speaking base in the EU. What surprises most Lao newcomers first is the cold and the wind, and the way daily life keeps going outdoors regardless of the weather.

Permission to stay beyond 90 daysYes, needs a permit or scheme, then an IRP
Lao licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementNo
Social security agreementNo
PetsUnlisted country, rabies blood test

Do you need a visa?

Yes. Lao citizens are visa required, so you need an Irish visa before you travel and then an immigration permission to stay. For a move the visa is a long stay D visa, applied for online through AVATS and submitted with your passport and documents to the Irish embassy or visa office that covers Laos, or through its VFS partner where one is used. Allow at least eight weeks. The visa gets you to the border; your permission to live here comes from the permit, course or family relationship behind it. You cannot enter on a short stay C visa and switch to a work permission from inside Ireland.

  • Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit, and you can apply for Stamp 4 after two years.
  • General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants, home carers, chefs and construction trades come in on this permit.
  • Stamp 2 study permission for a degree or a recognised English language course, with the right to work 20 hours a week in term time (40 in the holidays). Graduates of Irish degrees get the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) to look for work for one to two years.
  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere. Malaysia has sent students and professionals to Ireland for generations, especially in medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, engineering, accountancy and tech, and Irish universities remain a well-trodden path for Malaysian medical students in particular. Dublin, Cork and Galway all have Malaysian graduates who stayed on in hospitals, pharma and global tech firms, while Kuala Lumpur's professionals see Ireland as an easy English-speaking base within the EU. Family links from earlier generations of students bring others. What surprises most Malaysians first is how early restaurants close and how hard it is to find a good meal late at night.

Quick factsMalaysia to IrelandVisa to enterNo, up to 90 daysPermission to stay beyond 90 daysYes, needs a permit or scheme, then an IRPMalaysian licence exchangeableNoDouble taxation agreementYesSocial security agreementNoPetsListed country, no blood test

Do you need a visa?

Malaysian citizens are not visa required, so you can enter Ireland for up to 90 days without applying for anything. Staying longer is a different matter: you need an immigration permission before the 90 days run out, and you cannot turn a visit into a job from inside the country except through a handful of schemes. Get the permit or the college place sorted first, then travel. Ireland has added visa requirements for several countries since 2022, so check the current list on irishimmigration.ie before you book.

Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit, and you can apply for Stamp 4 after two years.General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants, home carers, chefs and construction trades come in on this permit.Stamp 2 study permission for a degree or a recognised English language course, with the right to work 20 hours a week in term time (40 in the holidays). Graduates of Irish degrees get the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) to look for work for one to two years.Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.Stamp 0 for retirees and people of independent means, with income of around 50,000 euro a year per person and private medical insurance, and no right to work.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere. If you have an Irish born parent or grandparent, check the Foreign Births Register first, because once registered you are an Irish citizen and none of the above applies.

Finding work and getting your qualifications recognised

Most Malaysians arrive with fluent English from school and work, so interviews are rarely a problem beyond adjusting to Irish accents and slang. Employers do not usually ask for IELTS, though registration bodies and universities may. Irish is on signs but not needed.

Because most routes need a job offer first, the search happens from home. Irish CVs run to two pages, carry no photo and no date of birth, and lead with what you did rather than your job title. Most hiring runs through LinkedIn, IrishJobs, Jobs.ie and the employers' own sites; agencies are strong in tech, finance, pharma and healthcare, and employers used to sponsoring permits say so in the advert. Get your degree assessed by NARIC Ireland (free, through QQI) before you apply; it maps a Malaysian qualification onto the Irish framework and employers recognise the letter. Regulated professions register with their own body: nurses with NMBI, doctors with the Medical Council, teachers with the Teaching Council, engineers with Engineers Ireland, and physiotherapists, radiographers and social workers with CORU. Those bodies, not employers, are the ones that ask for an English test.

Your driving licence

Malaysia is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so you cannot swap a Malaysian licence for an Irish one. You can drive on your Malaysian licence for up to 12 months as a visitor, ideally with an International Driving Permit, but once you are resident you must go through the Irish process: pass the driver theory test, get a learner permit, complete Essential Driver Training and pass the driving test. The good news is that experienced foreign licence holders only need 6 EDT lessons instead of 12 and can skip the usual six month wait before the test. Learner permit holders must be accompanied by a full licence holder, which is the part that catches people out. Remember that Ireland drives on the left.

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and Malaysia have a double taxation agreement, so income taxed in one country is generally credited in the other and the treaty decides which country taxes what. You become Irish tax resident after 183 days in a tax year (or 280 days over two years), and from then Ireland taxes your worldwide income, with credit for Malaysian tax under the treaty. Register with Revenue through myAccount as soon as you have a PPS number so your employer taxes you correctly, and tell the Malaysian tax authority that you are leaving.

There is no social security agreement between Ireland and Malaysia, so the two records stand alone. You need at least 520 paid PRSI contributions (ten years) to qualify for any Irish State Pension (Contributory), and the full rate takes 40 years of contributions. Check whether your Malaysian state pension can be paid to you in Ireland, and whether you can keep contributing voluntarily from abroad.

Your credit history does not follow you. Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so expect to build a record from scratch before a mortgage or car loan. Moving money from the ringgit into euro is cheapest through a specialist transfer provider rather than a bank; open the Irish account first, because you need an Irish IBAN to receive salary.

Healthcare

Ireland has a public system run by the HSE, but it is not free at the point of use. Once you are ordinarily resident (living in Ireland or intending to for at least a year) you use public hospitals as a public patient, and inpatient charges were abolished in April 2023. A GP visit costs roughly 50 to 70 euro unless you qualify for a medical card or GP visit card on income grounds (children under 8 get GP visits free), and prescriptions are paid for up to a monthly cap under the Drugs Payment Scheme. Emergency departments charge 100 euro without a GP referral. Students, Stamp 0 holders and most visa applicants must show private medical insurance, so many people arrive with a policy already.

Around half the population holds private health insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health, mainly to shorten waiting lists. If you are 35 or older, buy it within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading. Register with a GP as soon as you have an address; practices in Dublin often have closed lists, so ask several.

Goods arriving from Malaysia are imports from outside the EU. You can bring your household belongings free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for at least 12 months and owned the goods for at least 6 months; your removals company files the declaration and you cannot sell the goods for a year. A car qualifies for VRT relief on the same terms, but shipping a car from Malaysia rarely makes sense once freight, registration and Irish insurance are added up.

Malaysia is a listed country under the EU pet rules, so no rabies blood test is needed. Your dog, cat or ferret needs a microchip, a rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, an EU animal health certificate issued by an official vet within 10 days of travel, and for dogs a tapeworm treatment 24 to 120 hours before arrival. Pets from outside the EU must arrive as manifest cargo or with an approved airline on an approved route (Dublin Airport handles most), and are checked on arrival.

Kuala Lumpur's heat and humidity give way to cool, wet weather and winter days that end mid-afternoon, while summer evenings stay light until late. Renting is formal and competitive, groceries and eating out cost more, and mamak stalls and hawker centres have no equivalent. Cards dominate, driving on the left is familiar, and pubs replace late-night food as the default social venue.

There are no regular direct flights between Dublin and Malaysia, so getting home usually means one stop, most often via Dubai, Doha, Abu Dhabi, Istanbul, London or Amsterdam; budget for the time as well as the fare.

articles.description: Pakistan has a long-standing and growing connection with Ireland, built on doctors and nurses in Irish hospitals, students in IT, engineering, business…
articles.previewHtml:
Pakistan has a long-standing and growing connection with Ireland, built on doctors and nurses in Irish hospitals, students in IT, engineering, business and medicine, tech professionals in Dublin's global firms, and families joining relatives already settled here. Irish medical training and hospitals have drawn Pakistani doctors for generations, while graduates from Lahore, Karachi and Islamabad now also arrive in software, data and accountancy roles. Hospitality, retail and taxi work provide other footholds. What surprises most Pakistanis first is how informal Irish workplaces are, with senior consultants and managers addressed by first name and hierarchy kept quiet.

Quick factsPakistan to Ireland
Visa to enterYes, long stay D visa
Permission to stay beyond 90 daysYes, needs a permit or scheme, then an IRP
Pakistani licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementYes
Social security agreementNo
PetsUnlisted country, rabies blood test

Do you need a visa?

Yes. Pakistani citizens are visa required, so you need an Irish visa before you travel and then an immigration permission to stay. For a move the visa is a long stay D visa, applied for online through AVATS and submitted with your passport and documents to the Irish embassy or visa office that covers Pakistan, or through its VFS partner where one is used. Allow at least eight weeks. The visa gets you to the border; your permission to live here comes from the permit, course or family relationship behind it. You cannot enter on a short stay C visa and switch to a work permission from inside Ireland.

  • Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit, and you can apply for Stamp 4 after two years.
  • General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants, home carers, chefs and construction trades come in on this permit.
  • Stamp 2 study permission for a degree or a recognised English language course, with the right to work 20 hours a week in term time (40 in the holidays). Graduates of Irish degrees get the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) to look for work for one to two years.
  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere. If you have an Irish born parent or grandparent, check the Foreign Births Register first, because once registered you are an Irish citizen and none of the above applies.

Finding work and getting your qualifications recognised

Most Pakistanis arrive with strong English from school, university and professional life, so interviews are rarely a problem beyond adjusting to Irish accents and understatement. Employers do not usually ask for IELTS, though registration bodies and universities may. Irish is on signs but not needed.

Because most routes need a job offer first, the search happens from home. Irish CVs run to two pages, carry no photo and no date of birth, and lead with what you did rather than your job title. Most hiring runs through LinkedIn, IrishJobs, Jobs.ie and the employers' own sites; agencies are strong in tech, finance, pharma and healthcare, and employers used to sponsoring permits say so in the advert. Get your degree assessed by NARIC Ireland (free, through QQI) before you apply; it maps a Pakistani qualification onto the Irish framework and employers recognise the letter. Regulated professions register with their own body: nurses with NMBI, doctors with the Medical Council, teachers with the Teaching Council, engineers with Engineers Ireland, and physiotherapists, radiographers and social workers with CORU. Those bodies, not employers, are the ones that ask for an English test.

Your driving licence

Pakistan is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so you cannot swap a Pakistani licence for an Irish one. You can drive on your Pakistani licence for up to 12 months as a visitor, ideally with an International Driving Permit, but once you are resident you must go through the Irish process: pass the driver theory test, get a learner permit, complete Essential Driver Training and pass the driving test. The good news is that experienced foreign licence holders only need 6 EDT lessons instead of 12 and can skip the usual six month wait before the test. Learner permit holders must be accompanied by a full licence holder, which is the part that catches people out. Remember that Ireland drives on the left.

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and Pakistan have a double taxation agreement, so income taxed in one country is generally credited in the other and the treaty decides which country taxes what. You become Irish tax resident after 183 days in a tax year (or 280 days over two years), and from then Ireland taxes your worldwide income, with credit for Pakistani tax under the treaty. Register with Revenue through myAccount as soon as you have a PPS number so your employer taxes you correctly, and tell the Pakistani tax authority that you are leaving.

There is no social security agreement between Ireland and Pakistan, so the two records stand alone. You need at least 520 paid PRSI contributions (ten years) to qualify for any Irish State Pension (Contributory), and the full rate takes 40 years of contributions. Check whether your Pakistani state pension can be paid to you in Ireland, and whether you can keep contributing voluntarily from abroad.

Your credit history does not follow you. Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so expect to build a record from scratch before a mortgage or car loan. Moving money from the Pakistani rupee into euro is cheapest through a specialist transfer provider rather than a bank; open the Irish account first, because you need an Irish IBAN to receive salary. Pakistan has exchange controls, so check what you are allowed to take out and the paperwork needed before you leave, and bring evidence of the source of funds for the Irish bank.

Ireland has a public system run by the HSE, but it is not free at the point of use. Once you are ordinarily resident (living in Ireland or intending to for at least a year) you use public hospitals as a public patient, and inpatient charges were abolished in April 2023. A GP visit costs roughly 50 to 70 euro unless you qualify for a medical card or GP visit card on income grounds (children under 8 get GP visits free), and prescriptions are paid for up to a monthly cap under the Drugs Payment Scheme. Emergency departments charge 100 euro without a GP referral. Students, Stamp 0 holders and most visa applicants must show private medical insurance, so many people arrive with a policy already.

Around half the population holds private health insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health, mainly to shorten waiting lists. If you are 35 or older, buy it within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading. Register with a GP as soon as you have an address; practices in Dublin often have closed lists, so ask several.

Goods arriving from Pakistan are imports from outside the EU. You can bring your household belongings free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for at least 12 months and owned the goods for at least 6 months; your removals company files the declaration and you cannot sell the goods for a year. A car qualifies for VRT relief on the same terms, but shipping a car from Pakistan rarely makes sense once freight, registration and Irish insurance are added up.

Pakistan is an unlisted country under the EU pet rules, which adds a blood test. Your dog, cat or ferret needs a microchip, then a rabies vaccination, then a rabies antibody titre test at least 30 days after the vaccination at an EU approved laboratory, and then a three month wait from the date of the blood sample before travel. Add an EU animal health certificate issued within 10 days of travel and, for dogs, a tapeworm treatment 24 to 120 hours before arrival. Pets must arrive as manifest cargo or with an approved airline on an approved route (Dublin Airport handles most). Start the process at least four months before you fly.

Settling in: community and daily life

The Pakistani community in Ireland is large, well established and spread well beyond Dublin into Cork, Limerick, Galway and towns with regional hospitals. Newcomers find each other through mosques and Islamic centres, Pakistani community and professional associations, cricket clubs, Eid and Independence Day gatherings, and active Facebook and WhatsApp groups.

Pakistan's hot summers and short, mild winters are replaced by cool rain in every season and winter afternoons that go dark early, with long bright summer evenings in return. Renting is formal and competitive, groceries and eating out cost more, and halal options need some planning outside larger cities. Cards dominate over cash, pubs anchor social life even for non-drinkers, and driving on the left is familiar.

There are no regular direct flights between Dublin and Pakistan, so getting home usually means one stop, most often via Dubai, Doha, Abu Dhabi, Istanbul, London or Amsterdam; budget for the time as well as the fare.

  • Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie with your passport and proof of Irish address.
  • Register for your Irish Residence Permit within 90 days (300 euro); book the appointment the week you land because slots fill up.
  • Register with Revenue myAccount once you have a PPS number so your employer can tax you correctly.
  • Open an Irish bank account; a utility bill, tenancy agreement or employer letter usually counts as proof of address.
  • Register with a GP and, if you want it, buy private health insurance within 9 months.
  • Get a Leap card for public transport and book the driver theory test if you plan to drive.
  • If a pet is following later, get its rabies blood test done now so the three month clock is running.

Finding work and getting your qualifications recognised

Singaporeans arrive with fluent English, so language is no barrier in interviews; employers will not ask for IELTS, though universities and professional registration bodies may. The adjustment is to Irish accents and slang rather than the language, and Irish is on signs but not needed.

Because most routes need a job offer first, the search happens from home. Irish CVs run to two pages, carry no photo and no date of birth, and lead with what you did rather than your job title. Those bodies, not employers, are the ones that ask for an English test.

Singapore is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so you cannot swap a Singaporean licence for an Irish one. Register with Revenue through myAccount as soon as you have a PPS number so your employer taxes you correctly, and tell the Singaporean tax authority that you are leaving.

Moving money from the Singapore dollar into euro is cheapest through a specialist transfer provider rather than a bank; open the Irish account first, because you need an Irish IBAN to receive salary.

Ireland has a public system run by the HSE, but it is not free at the point of use. Once you are ordinarily resident (living in Ireland or intending to for at least a year) you use public hospitals as a public patient, and inpatient charges were abolished in April 2023. Register with a GP as soon as you have an address; practices in Dublin often have closed lists, so ask several.

articles.description: South Korea sends a growing number of people to Ireland for English-language study, working holidays, university exchanges and jobs in tech, finance…

South Korea sends a growing number of people to Ireland for English-language study, working holidays, university exchanges and jobs in tech, finance, pharma, semiconductors and engineering, with Dublin's global tech firms hiring Korean speakers for market and customer roles. Seoul's graduates value Ireland as an English-speaking EU base that feels friendlier and smaller than London, and Korean investment in Irish tech and manufacturing adds professional moves. Marriage, curiosity about Europe and postgraduate research bring others. What surprises most Koreans first is how slow and relaxed service, deliveries and workplaces are compared with Seoul's speed.

Quick factsSouth Korea to Ireland
Visa to enterNo, up to 90 days
Permission to stay beyond 90 daysYes, needs a permit or scheme, then an IRP
South Korean licence exchangeableYes, exchange without a test
Double taxation agreementYes
Social security agreementYes, bilateral agreement
Working Holiday AuthorisationYes
PetsUnlisted country, rabies blood test

Do you need a visa?

South Korean citizens are not visa required, so you can enter Ireland for up to 90 days without applying for anything. Staying longer is a different matter: you need an immigration permission before the 90 days run out, and you cannot turn a visit into a job from inside the country except through a handful of schemes. Get the permit or the college place sorted first, then travel. Ireland has added visa requirements for several countries since 2022, so check the current list on irishimmigration.ie before you book.

  • Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit, and you can apply for Stamp 4 after two years.
  • General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants, home carers, chefs and construction trades come in on this permit.
  • Working Holiday Authorisation: Ireland has a working holiday agreement with South Korea, which lets young South Korean citizens (typically 18 to 30 or 35) live and work in Ireland for up to 12 months without a job offer. Apply through the Irish embassy that covers South Korea; places are limited each year.

  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.
  • Stamp 0 for retirees and people of independent means, with income of around 50,000 euro a year per person and private medical insurance, and no right to work.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere.   • Register with Revenue myAccount once you have a PPS number so your employer can tax you correctly.

articles.description: Sri Lanka has a long-standing connection with Ireland through doctors, nurses and engineers, and now sends students in IT, business, hospitality and…
articles.previewHtml:
Sri Lanka has a long-standing connection with Ireland through doctors, nurses and engineers, and now sends students in IT, business, hospitality and nursing, tech professionals, accountants, chefs and care workers, as well as families joining relatives already here. Colombo's graduates see Ireland as an English-speaking EU alternative to Australia and the UK, and Irish hospitals and universities are familiar destinations for medical and nursing careers. Social security agreementNo
PetsUnlisted country, rabies blood test

For a move the visa is a long stay D visa, applied for online through AVATS and submitted with your passport and documents to the Irish embassy or visa office that covers Sri Lanka, or through its VFS partner where one is used. Allow at least eight weeks. The visa gets you to the border; your permission to live here comes from the permit, course or family relationship behind it. You cannot enter on a short stay C visa and switch to a work permission from inside Ireland.

  • Stamp 2 study permission for a degree or a recognised English language course, with the right to work 20 hours a week in term time (40 in the holidays). Graduates of Irish degrees get the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) to look for work for one to two years.
  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere. If you have an Irish born parent or grandparent, check the Foreign Births Register first, because once registered you are an Irish citizen and none of the above applies.

Most Sri Lankan professionals and students arrive with good English from school and university, though spoken confidence and Irish accents take time. Employers rarely ask for IELTS, but universities and nursing and medical registration bodies usually do. Irish is on signs but not needed.

Because most routes need a job offer first, the search happens from home. Irish CVs run to two pages, carry no photo and no date of birth, and lead with what you did rather than your job title. Most hiring runs through LinkedIn, IrishJobs, Jobs.ie and the employers' own sites; agencies are strong in tech, finance, pharma and healthcare, and employers used to sponsoring permits say so in the advert. Get your degree assessed by NARIC Ireland (free, through QQI) before you apply; it maps a Sri Lankan qualification onto the Irish framework and employers recognise the letter. Those bodies, not employers, are the ones that ask for an English test.

Your driving licence

Sri Lanka is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so you cannot swap a Sri Lankan licence for an Irish one. You can drive on your Sri Lankan licence for up to 12 months as a visitor, ideally with an International Driving Permit, but once you are resident you must go through the Irish process: pass the driver theory test, get a learner permit, complete Essential Driver Training and pass the driving test. Marriage and a fondness for Irish music and landscape bring some too. Double taxation agreementNo
Social security agreementNo
Working Holiday AuthorisationYes
PetsListed country, no blood test

Taiwanese citizens are not visa required, so you can enter Ireland for up to 90 days without applying for anything. Staying longer is a different matter: you need an immigration permission before the 90 days run out, and you cannot turn a visit into a job from inside the country except through a handful of schemes.   • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.
  • Stamp 0 for retirees and people of independent means, with income of around 50,000 euro a year per person and private medical insurance, and no right to work.

articles.previewHtml:
Tajikistan sends only a handful of people to Ireland each year, and most arrive for a specific reason rather than along a well-worn route: a postgraduate place at an Irish university, a job in tech or engineering, or joining a partner who is already here. Some come through international scholarship schemes, others combine study with work in hospitality. What tends to surprise Tajiks most is the flatness and wetness of the Irish landscape after a country defined by high mountains and dry summers.

Quick factsTajikistan to Ireland
Visa to enterYes, long stay D visa
Permission to stay beyond 90 daysYes, needs a permit or scheme, then an IRP
Tajik licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementNo
Social security agreementNo
PetsUnlisted country, rabies blood test

Do you need a visa?

Yes. Tajik citizens are visa required, so you need an Irish visa before you travel and then an immigration permission to stay. For a move the visa is a long stay D visa, applied for online through AVATS and submitted with your passport and documents to the Irish embassy or visa office that covers Tajikistan, or through its VFS partner where one is used. Allow at least eight weeks. The visa gets you to the border; your permission to live here comes from the permit, course or family relationship behind it. You cannot enter on a short stay C visa and switch to a work permission from inside Ireland.

  • Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit, and you can apply for Stamp 4 after two years.
  • General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants, home carers, chefs and construction trades come in on this permit.
  • Stamp 2 study permission for a degree or a recognised English language course, with the right to work 20 hours a week in term time (40 in the holidays). Graduates of Irish degrees get the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) to look for work for one to two years.
  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere. If you have an Irish born parent or grandparent, check the Foreign Births Register first, because once registered you are an Irish citizen and none of the above applies.

Finding work and getting your qualifications recognised

English usually comes after Tajik and Russian, so brushing up before interviews pays off; employers judge you in conversation rather than by certificate, though universities and registration bodies may ask for IELTS. Irish appears on signs but you will not need it.

Because most routes need a job offer first, the search happens from home. Irish CVs run to two pages, carry no photo and no date of birth, and lead with what you did rather than your job title. Most hiring runs through LinkedIn, IrishJobs, Jobs.ie and the employers' own sites; agencies are strong in tech, finance, pharma and healthcare, and employers used to sponsoring permits say so in the advert. Get your degree assessed by NARIC Ireland (free, through QQI) before you apply; it maps a Tajik qualification onto the Irish framework and employers recognise the letter. Regulated professions register with their own body: nurses with NMBI, doctors with the Medical Council, teachers with the Teaching Council, engineers with Engineers Ireland, and physiotherapists, radiographers and social workers with CORU. Those bodies, not employers, are the ones that ask for an English test.

Your driving licence

Tajikistan is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so you cannot swap a Tajik licence for an Irish one. You can drive on your Tajik licence for up to 12 months as a visitor, ideally with an International Driving Permit, but once you are resident you must go through the Irish process: pass the driver theory test, get a learner permit, complete Essential Driver Training and pass the driving test. The good news is that experienced foreign licence holders only need 6 EDT lessons instead of 12 and can skip the usual six month wait before the test. Learner permit holders must be accompanied by a full licence holder, which is the part that catches people out. Remember that Ireland drives on the left.

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and Tajikistan have no double taxation agreement. For most people this matters less than it sounds: once you become Irish tax resident (183 days in a tax year, or 280 over two) and your job is here, Irish PAYE applies to your salary and your Tajik tax obligations usually end with your residence there. It matters if you keep Tajik income, such as rent or a business, which could be taxed in both countries; Revenue may grant unilateral relief for foreign tax paid, and a tax adviser is worth it in that case. Register with Revenue through myAccount as soon as you have a PPS number.

There is no social security agreement between Ireland and Tajikistan, so the two records stand alone. You need at least 520 paid PRSI contributions (ten years) to qualify for any Irish State Pension (Contributory), and the full rate takes 40 years of contributions. Check whether your Tajik state pension can be paid to you in Ireland, and whether you can keep contributing voluntarily from abroad.

Your credit history does not follow you. Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so expect to build a record from scratch before a mortgage or car loan. Moving money from the somoni into euro is cheapest through a specialist transfer provider rather than a bank; open the Irish account first, because you need an Irish IBAN to receive salary.

Healthcare

Ireland has a public system run by the HSE, but it is not free at the point of use. Once you are ordinarily resident (living in Ireland or intending to for at least a year) you use public hospitals as a public patient, and inpatient charges were abolished in April 2023. A GP visit costs roughly 50 to 70 euro unless you qualify for a medical card or GP visit card on income grounds (children under 8 get GP visits free), and prescriptions are paid for up to a monthly cap under the Drugs Payment Scheme. Emergency departments charge 100 euro without a GP referral. Students, Stamp 0 holders and most visa applicants must show private medical insurance, so many people arrive with a policy already.

Around half the population holds private health insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health, mainly to shorten waiting lists. If you are 35 or older, buy it within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading. Register with a GP as soon as you have an address; practices in Dublin often have closed lists, so ask several.

Bringing your things and your pet

Goods arriving from Tajikistan are imports from outside the EU. You can bring your household belongings free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for at least 12 months and owned the goods for at least 6 months; your removals company files the declaration and you cannot sell the goods for a year. A car qualifies for VRT relief on the same terms, but shipping a car from Tajikistan rarely makes sense once freight, registration and Irish insurance are added up.

Tajikistan is an unlisted country under the EU pet rules, which adds a blood test. Your dog, cat or ferret needs a microchip, then a rabies vaccination, then a rabies antibody titre test at least 30 days after the vaccination at an EU approved laboratory, and then a three month wait from the date of the blood sample before travel. Add an EU animal health certificate issued within 10 days of travel and, for dogs, a tapeworm treatment 24 to 120 hours before arrival. Pets must arrive as manifest cargo or with an approved airline on an approved route (Dublin Airport handles most). Start the process at least four months before you fly.

Settling in: community and daily life

The Tajik community in Ireland is very small and recent, with no formal association of its own; most people are in Dublin, often connected to a university. Newcomers usually find each other through wider Central Asian and Russian-speaking networks, Muslim community centres, and Telegram or WhatsApp groups rather than anything specifically Tajik.

Daily life in Ireland is mild, damp and cloudy for much of the year, with long summer evenings and short winter days that take some getting used to. Most people rent through online listings and viewings are competitive, so be ready to move fast. Card payments are the norm almost everywhere, driving is on the left, and social life often revolves around the pub.

There are no regular direct flights between Dublin and Tajikistan, so getting home usually means one stop, most often via Dubai, Doha, Abu Dhabi, Istanbul, London or Amsterdam; budget for the time as well as the fare.

  • Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie with your passport and proof of Irish address.
  • Register for your Irish Residence Permit within 90 days (300 euro); book the appointment the week you land because slots fill up.
  • Register with Revenue myAccount once you have a PPS number so your employer can tax you correctly.
  • Open an Irish bank account; a utility bill, tenancy agreement or employer letter usually counts as proof of address.
  • Register with a GP and, if you want it, buy private health insurance within 9 months.
  • Get a Leap card for public transport and book the driver theory test if you plan to drive.
  • If a pet is following later, get its rabies blood test done now so the three month clock is running.

  • NARIC Ireland: qualification recognition
  • National Driver Licence Service

Timor-Leste has one of the smallest migrant flows to Ireland of any country, and those who come usually do so for study, often on scholarships to Irish universities, or for work in healthcare and hospitality, sometimes via family already settled in Britain or Northern Ireland. There is also a long-standing goodwill between the two countries dating from Ireland's support for Timorese independence, which some arrivals mention. What surprises Timorese newcomers most is the daylight: long, bright summer evenings and then winter afternoons that go dark before the working day ends.

Visa to enterYes, long stay D visa
Permission to stay beyond 90 daysYes, needs a permit or scheme, then an IRP
Timorese licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementNo
Social security agreementNo
PetsUnlisted country, rabies blood test

Do you need a visa?

Yes. Timorese citizens are visa required, so you need an Irish visa before you travel and then an immigration permission to stay. For a move the visa is a long stay D visa, applied for online through AVATS and submitted with your passport and documents to the Irish embassy or visa office that covers Timor-Leste, or through its VFS partner where one is used. Allow at least eight weeks. The visa gets you to the border; your permission to live here comes from the permit, course or family relationship behind it. You cannot enter on a short stay C visa and switch to a work permission from inside Ireland.

  • Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit, and you can apply for Stamp 4 after two years.
  • General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants, home carers, chefs and construction trades come in on this permit.
  • Stamp 2 study permission for a degree or a recognised English language course, with the right to work 20 hours a week in term time (40 in the holidays). Graduates of Irish degrees get the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) to look for work for one to two years.
  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere. If you have an Irish born parent or grandparent, check the Foreign Births Register first, because once registered you are an Irish citizen and none of the above applies.

Allow at least eight weeks. The visa gets you to the border; your permission to live here comes from the permit, course or family relationship behind it. You cannot enter on a short stay C visa and switch to a work permission from inside Ireland.

Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit, and you can apply for Stamp 4 after two years.General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Graduates of Irish degrees get the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) to look for work for one to two years.Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere. If you have an Irish born parent or grandparent, check the Foreign Births Register first, because once registered you are an Irish citizen and none of the above applies.

English usually sits behind Turkmen and Russian, so conversation practice before interviews pays off; employers judge how you communicate rather than a certificate, though universities and registration bodies may ask for IELTS. Irish appears on signs but is not needed.

Because most routes need a job offer first, the search happens from home. Irish CVs run to two pages, carry no photo and no date of birth, and lead with what you did rather than your job title. articles.previewHtml:
New Zealand and Ireland have a long habit of swapping people, and Kiwis come here for tech and finance jobs in Dublin, for medicine and nursing, for construction and engineering, for a stint of rugby, and because many have Irish grandparents and want to see where the family came from. Ireland is also a handy base for exploring Europe on weekends. What surprises New Zealanders most is how close everything is: a drive that would be a serious road trip at home crosses the whole island before lunch.

Quick factsNew Zealand to Ireland
Visa to enterNo, up to 90 days
Permission to stay beyond 90 daysYes, needs a permit or scheme, then an IRP
New Zealand licence exchangeableYes, exchange without a test
Double taxation agreementYes
Social security agreementYes, bilateral agreement
Working Holiday AuthorisationYes
PetsListed country, no blood test

Do you need a visa?

New Zealand citizens are not visa required, so you can enter Ireland for up to 90 days without applying for anything. Staying longer is a different matter: you need an immigration permission before the 90 days run out, and you cannot turn a visit into a job from inside the country except through a handful of schemes. Get the permit or the college place sorted first, then travel. Ireland has added visa requirements for several countries since 2022, so check the current list on irishimmigration.ie before you book.

  • Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit, and you can apply for Stamp 4 after two years.
  • General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants, home carers, chefs and construction trades come in on this permit.
  • Working Holiday Authorisation: Ireland has a working holiday agreement with New Zealand, which lets young New Zealand citizens (typically 18 to 30 or 35) live and work in Ireland for up to 12 months without a job offer. Apply through the Irish embassy that covers New Zealand; places are limited each year.
  • Stamp 2 study permission for a degree or a recognised English language course, with the right to work 20 hours a week in term time (40 in the holidays). Graduates of Irish degrees get the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) to look for work for one to two years.
  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.
  • Stamp 0 for retirees and people of independent means, with income of around 50,000 euro a year per person and private medical insurance, and no right to work.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere. If you have an Irish born parent or grandparent, check the Foreign Births Register first, because once registered you are an Irish citizen and none of the above applies.

You will have no language barrier, only vocabulary and accent: Irish colleagues will spot the Kiwi vowels immediately and you will pick up grand, craic and yer man within a week. Irish appears on signs but nobody expects you to speak it.

Because most routes need a job offer first, the search happens from home. Irish CVs run to two pages, carry no photo and no date of birth, and lead with what you did rather than your job title. Most hiring runs through LinkedIn, IrishJobs, Jobs.ie and the employers' own sites; agencies are strong in tech, finance, pharma and healthcare, and employers used to sponsoring permits say so in the advert. Get your degree assessed by NARIC Ireland (free, through QQI) before you apply; it maps a New Zealand qualification onto the Irish framework and employers recognise the letter. Regulated professions register with their own body: nurses with NMBI, doctors with the Medical Council, teachers with the Teaching Council, engineers with Engineers Ireland, and physiotherapists, radiographers and social workers with CORU. Those bodies, not employers, are the ones that ask for an English test.

Your driving licence

New Zealand is on the NDLS list of recognised states, so a full New Zealand licence can be exchanged for an Irish one without a theory or driving test. You can drive on the New Zealand licence for up to 12 months after becoming resident, then you must exchange it. Apply online at ndls.ie if you have a Public Services Card and MyGovID, or book an NDLS centre appointment. Bring the licence, a certified English translation if it is not in English, proof of your PPS number, proof of address and photo ID; you may also need a letter of entitlement from the issuing authority. The fee is 65 euro, and the exchanged licence covers the categories that match Irish ones.

Ireland and New Zealand have a double taxation agreement, so income taxed in one country is generally credited in the other and the treaty decides which country taxes what. Once you are ordinarily resident (living in Ireland or intending to for at least a year) you use public hospitals as a public patient, and inpatient charges were abolished in April 2023. A GP visit costs roughly 50 to 70 euro unless you qualify for a medical card or GP visit card on income grounds (children under 8 get GP visits free), and prescriptions are paid for up to a monthly cap under the Drugs Payment Scheme. If you are 35 or older, buy it within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading. Register with a GP as soon as you have an address; practices in Dublin often have closed lists, so ask several.

Goods arriving from New Zealand are imports from outside the EU. You can bring your household belongings free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for at least 12 months and owned the goods for at least 6 months; your removals company files the declaration and you cannot sell the goods for a year. Pets from outside the EU must arrive as manifest cargo or with an approved airline on an approved route (Dublin Airport handles most), and are checked on arrival.

The New Zealand community in Ireland is small but long-standing, spread across Dublin and the larger cities, and blends easily into Irish life because so much is familiar. Newcomers usually find each other through rugby and GAA clubs, the New Zealand embassy's events, and Kiwis in Ireland Facebook groups where jobs, flats and Anzac Day plans circulate.

The climate is close enough to feel like home, but summers are cooler, winters darker, and the daylight swing is bigger than in most of New Zealand. Renting in Dublin is tighter and more competitive than you may be used to, groceries cost about what you would expect, eating out a little more. Driving on the left and the pub culture will feel entirely natural.

There are no regular direct flights between Dublin and New Zealand, so getting home usually means one stop, most often via Dubai, Doha, Singapore or Los Angeles; budget for the time as well as the fare.

  • Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie with your passport and proof of Irish address.
  • Register for your Irish Residence Permit within 90 days (300 euro); book the appointment the week you land because slots fill up.
  • Register with Revenue myAccount once you have a PPS number so your employer can tax you correctly.
  • Open an Irish bank account; a utility bill, tenancy agreement or employer letter usually counts as proof of address.
  • Register with a GP and, if you want it, buy private health insurance within 9 months.
  • Get a Leap card for public transport and book your licence exchange at the NDLS before the 12 months are up.

articles.previewHtml:
Papua New Guinea sends only a few people to Ireland, and most arrive for study, often on scholarships to Irish universities in fields like development, agriculture and public health, or for work in mining engineering, healthcare and the church. Some come via Australia, where they have already lived. Historic links between Irish missionaries and PNG mean the country is better known here than you might expect. What surprises Papua New Guinean arrivals most is the winter darkness and the cold that comes with it after a lifetime near the equator.

Quick factsPapua New Guinea to Ireland
Visa to enterYes, long stay D visa
Permission to stay beyond 90 daysYes, needs a permit or scheme, then an IRP
Papua New Guinean licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementNo
Social security agreementNo
PetsUnlisted country, rabies blood test

Do you need a visa?

Yes. Papua New Guinean citizens are visa required, so you need an Irish visa before you travel and then an immigration permission to stay. For a move the visa is a long stay D visa, applied for online through AVATS and submitted with your passport and documents to the Irish embassy or visa office that covers Papua New Guinea, or through its VFS partner where one is used. Allow at least eight weeks. The visa gets you to the border; your permission to live here comes from the permit, course or family relationship behind it. You cannot enter on a short stay C visa and switch to a work permission from inside Ireland.

  • Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit, and you can apply for Stamp 4 after two years.
  • General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after the employer runs a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants, home carers, chefs and construction trades come in on this permit.
  • Stamp 2 study permission for a degree or a recognised English language course, with the right to work 20 hours a week in term time (40 in the holidays). Graduates of Irish degrees get the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) to look for work for one to two years.
  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish citizen, an EU citizen exercising treaty rights, or a permit holder.

Whichever route you take, you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving: online in Dublin, or at the local Garda immigration office elsewhere. If you have an Irish born parent or grandparent, check the Foreign Births Register first, because once registered you are an Irish citizen and none of the above applies.

Finding work and getting your qualifications recognised

English is an official language in Papua New Guinea and most arrivals are fluent, so the adjustment is to Irish accents and slang rather than the language itself; universities and professional bodies may still ask for IELTS. Irish is on signs but not needed.

Because most routes need a job offer first, the search happens from home. Irish CVs run to two pages, carry no photo and no date of birth, and lead with what you did rather than your job title. Most hiring runs through LinkedIn, IrishJobs, Jobs.ie and the employers' own sites; agencies are strong in tech, finance, pharma and healthcare, and employers used to sponsoring permits say so in the advert. Get your degree assessed by NARIC Ireland (free, through QQI) before you apply; it maps a Papua New Guinean qualification onto the Irish framework and employers recognise the letter. Regulated professions register with their own body: nurses with NMBI, doctors with the Medical Council, teachers with the Teaching Council, engineers with Engineers Ireland, and physiotherapists, radiographers and social workers with CORU. Those bodies, not employers, are the ones that ask for an English test.

Your driving licence

Papua New Guinea is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so you cannot swap a Papua New Guinean licence for an Irish one. You can drive on your Papua New Guinean licence for up to 12 months as a visitor, ideally with an International Driving Permit, but once you are resident you must go through the Irish process: pass the driver theory test, get a learner permit, complete Essential Driver Training and pass the driving test. The good news is that experienced foreign licence holders only need 6 EDT lessons instead of 12 and can skip the usual six month wait before the test. Learner permit holders must be accompanied by a full licence holder, which is the part that catches people out. Remember that Ireland drives on the left.

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and Papua New Guinea have no double taxation agreement. For most people this matters less than it sounds: once you become Irish tax resident (183 days in a tax year, or 280 over two) and your job is here, Irish PAYE applies to your salary and your Papua New Guinean tax obligations usually end with your residence there. It matters if you keep Papua New Guinean income, such as rent or a business, which could be taxed in both countries; Revenue may grant unilateral relief for foreign tax paid, and a tax adviser is worth it in that case. Register with Revenue through myAccount as soon as you have a PPS number.

There is no social security agreement between Ireland and Papua New Guinea, so the two records stand alone.
